verdict: Avoid new wholesale-trade exposure in Patna for now; lend only to fast-turn staple/FMCG distributors with tight stock-and-receivable control, and decline discretionary or slow-moving goods traders.
title: Patna Wholesale Trade: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business actually is
**A Patna wholesaler buys stock, holds it in a godown, and sells on short credit to retailers and semi-wholesalers; cash is made on turnover and margin per cycle, not on price.** Value sits in inventory and receivables, so the whole credit case is how fast stock converts to cash and how reliably the retailer pays. CRISIL's trading-company criteria flag inventory obsolescence and receivable collection as the two core risks, especially where capital employed is small [9][10]. So when a proposal lands, check stock turns and receivable days first; if the borrower cannot show both, ask for the last twelve months of sales and collection registers.

## Where the cash sits and what has changed
**Bihar's GST collections fell 0.1% Apr-to-date against India's +6.1%, a 6.2 pp gap that says local trade volumes are flat to weak [D].** Against that, India-wide bank credit is up 29.1% YoY versus activity at +6.1% [D], and the repo is 5.5% on a tightening stance [D] — so money is available but priced to punish weak working-capital cycles. Local news is thin on wholesale specifically: a Vegfed outlet near Chidiya Ghar gate 2 selling 38 vegetable varieties direct from farmers with home delivery [1] signals organised, disintermediated retail creeping into Patna's fresh trade. Commercial LPG is costlier from Delhi to Patna ahead of Diwali [2], which raises godown and transport costs for food and hospitality-linked wholesalers. A political quote on trader sentiment [3] is noise, not credit evidence.

## Where to grow
**Pursue staple-food, FMCG and pharma distributors whose retailers reorder weekly and whose stock is not fashion- or season-dependent.** Peer results support the channel: Aditya Birla Lifestyle's wholesale channel grew 18% in Q2FY27 [7], and Mishka Exim's June 2026 net sales rose 234.87% YoY on trading volumes, though gross margin was only 11.5% [5] — thin margins mean volume discipline matters more than growth talk. Avoid garment, mobile and other short-life-cycle stock [9], and avoid traders selling into the fresh-vegetable chain that Vegfed is now entering directly [1].

## How to grow safely
**Structure every line as a stock-and-book-debt facility with monthly stock statements and receivables ageing, not a clean cash-credit limit.** Take monthly GST returns, top-ten debtor list and godown stock photos; require receivables to be insured or backed by post-dated cheques where the book is small [10]. Price for the 5.5% repo [D] and keep tenors short.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch for falling stock turns, rising receivable days and any drop in monthly GST turnover — these precede default in trading.** If a borrower's GST filings show two consecutive months of decline while bank credit grows, cut the limit. If a large retailer buyer delays payment beyond agreed terms, ask for the buyer's confirmation directly.
watch: Two consecutive months of falling turnover -> freeze fresh drawings and review limit
Stock turns slowing or stock older than 90 days -> demand liquidation plan or reduce limit
Top debtor past due beyond agreed terms -> seek direct confirmation and shift to cash/advance sales
Repo moves above 5.5% -> reprice facility and shorten tenor [D]
New direct-from-farmer outlet in borrower's category -> reassess demand and margin assumptions [1]
